title: Normalize lexical paths without canceling unresolved parents
goal: Repair normalize_segments(path), where path is a string. Perform lexical normalization using '/' as the only separator; never access the filesystem. A path starting with '/' is absolute. Ignore empty segments from repeated slashes and segments exactly '.'. A '..' cancels the immediately preceding surviving ordinary segment. If no ordinary segment can be canceled, preserve '..' in a relative path, including repeated leading '..'; absolute paths cannot go above root, so ignore those unresolved parents. A previous unresolved '..' must never be canceled by a later '..'. Preserve the spelling and order of all surviving ordinary segments, including whitespace, backslashes, and names such as '...'. Join with single slashes and remove trailing slash except for root. An empty normalized absolute path is '/'; an empty normalized relative path is '.'. Return a string, preserve the signature, and do not mutate inputs.
constraints: Do not add files, dependencies, or modify tests.
Keep normalize_segments and its signature unchanged.

provenance.hidden_tests: Distinct inputs exercising the same stated specification
